clusters.description: Running live service agents day to day: translating procedures into agent workflows, owning the content they draw on, writing what they must never answer and when they hand off, testing changes, reviewing conversations and stepping into live ones
clusters.bundling_evidence: Five postings carry most of this bundle under one person: D844 (owns the agent, its content, its guardrails and weekly conversation review: R5303, R3481, R9635, R1848), D826/D638 (translate SOPs into agent workflows, monitor and tune, own escalation paths: R3379, R9622, R9678, R1600), D775 (watch live conversations, decide when to intervene, QA new features: R4703, R5250, R1024), D282 and D324 (test and publish updates, triage broken or misrouted intents: R4041, R4652, R3583). Vendor admin guides attach the same knobs (handoff triggers R9416, escalation subagent R5876, routing R9479, escalation prompt R7901, test batches R1802, knowledge feed R8233, automated guardrail R8782) to an admin or knowledge manager. Shared decision: what the agent may answer and when it hands to a human.

outlook.reasons: Distinct by 2030: C1 already has stable titles in several postings (R9500, R5303, R1666, R4550) with its own decisions (what the agent must never answer and when it escalates, R9635, R9678) and content ownership (R3481, R8233), and seniority tiers are forming (2-3 years in R9500 vs 5-8 years portfolio in R4550). C7 gets distinct seats because vendors hard-code a human owner and a business sponsor per agent (R7070, R8345, R9271) and an approver for the agent portfolio (R4736, R3363); the sponsor half is the newest and least titled. C3's GTM Engineer is titled with a measure and a decision right (R9984, R7498). C10's legal engineer is titled at principal level (R3312) and the playbook-to-agent translation (R6915) needs legal judgment. Absorbed: code review and delegation stay with engineers holding merge rights (R4431, R5137, R3469); alert triage coaching attaches to existing analysts (R8757, R6522); accountants take the approve and override step (R8174, R2515); HR and regulated-firm oversight duties are legal obligations assigned to existing HR, compliance and model risk staff (R5394, R9009, R8958, R4013); function-embedded automation specialists (R3287, R3348, R7558) likely fold into function operations teams once tools are configurable by admins (R9237, R1002); approval policy ownership (C8, R6656, R7560) is likely absorbed into finance and procurement operations, though it may surface as its own seat because no record names who writes the policy the agent reads. Individual AI use (C13) is a skill, not a role (R2263, R7335). Workforce mix decisions (C14, R6160, R9974) land with HR and operations leaders. Automated: tier-1 service resolution (R3527, R7722, R6205, R1065), SDR qualification and outreach (R2486, R7643, R9524), matching, classification and reconciliation (R1762, R2771, R1324, R6952), routine information-processing micro-tasks (R9045, R7923, R5377) and manual batch testing of agents (R4295). Forward deployed engineering (R8825, R1642) and migration driving (R6438) look transitional. R3624 is unclustered: a single cross-industry survey line with no performer, decision, knowledge or doc partner.
